slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1960 census (April) carried to November 1960 along the 1950→1960 trend; white adults (21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii)) in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults), where poll taxes still applied in Alabama, Arkansas, Mississippi, Texas and Virginia; calibrated to certified 1960 returns.

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1960 comes out as it did: Kennedy wins, 303–219–15. The closest state was Hawaii, which went to Kennedy by 0.1 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1960 census counts and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1960 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

everyone.summary: 40.2 million more adults vote. California, Mississippi flip, but Kennedy still wins, 343–187–7. The closest call is Alaska, which holds for Nixon by 0.4 points. Nixon wins in 2 of 100 draws.

howIGotThis: What changed: Every adult can vote, and turns out.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: I'm worried about how we'll do if things don't pick up. The Democrats promise to get the economy moving again, and that matters to us out here.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: The economy's been sluggish these past few years. The fellow from Massachusetts seems to have plans to get things moving again. I'll likely vote for him tomorrow.
